title: Your smallest good deed may weigh like a mountain
subtitle: The Appreciative One who multiplies the little that we give
intro: Ash-Shakur (الشَّكُورُ) means the Most Appreciative, the One who values even the smallest good deed, rewards it far beyond its size and multiplies it many times over. It means nothing sincere you do for Him is ever too small to count.

root.sense: The Arabs called an animal shakur when it grew plump and gave plenty of milk on very little fodder: a little went a long way and showed. Shukr is recognising a favour and making it visible. When Allah is Shakur, a little from you becomes a great deal with Him.

row.title: Accepts and grows it
sub: Ten to seven hundred and more

row.title: A mountain of reward
sub: Found on the Day of Judgement

row.title: What I can do is too little

knowing: How can Allah be thankful when He needs nothing from us? We thank people because they met a need of ours; no one meets a need of His. {idea}His shukr is appreciation: He gives worth to deeds that, in themselves, are tiny, and then multiplies that worth.{/idea}

There are two names from this root. Ash-Shakir is the Appreciative. Ash-Shakur is the intensive form: the One who appreciates abundantly and constantly, so that an act you did not even notice yourself can become heavy in His scale. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever gives in charity the equal of a date from honest earnings, Allah accepts it with His right hand and raises it as one of you raises a foal, until it becomes like a mountain (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

His appreciation is unlike ours in another way. People notice the big gestures and forget the small ones. He notices the small ones and multiplies them. A good deed is written as ten up to seven hundred times and more, while a bad deed is written as one (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). {reward}It is a game you can only lose by refusing to play.{/reward}
seeing: The Prophet ﷺ told of a man who found a dog panting with thirst, climbed down a well, filled his shoe with water and gave it a drink. Allah thanked him for it and forgave him (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). {idea}A shoe full of water, appreciated by the Lord of the worlds.{/idea}

In Surah Fatir, Allah describes those who inherit the Book in three groups: one who wrongs himself, one in the middle, and one who races ahead in good, and He promises gardens to them (35:32-33). Around that passage He calls Himself Ghafur and Shakur twice (35:30, 35:34). He forgives much of our bad, appreciates the little of our good, and that is how imperfect people reach Paradise.

He calls charity a loan to Him and promises to multiply it, naming Himself Shakur and Halim (64:17). And when a pilgrim does more than is required between Safa and Marwa, the Quran reminds him that Allah is Shakir and Alim, appreciative of the extra and aware of the intention behind it (2:158).
trusting: Some days all you can manage is a short prayer, a few coins, a phone call to your mother. {trap}Discounting these as worthless is how shaytan talks people out of the good they can still do.{/trap} Ash-Shakur keeps the account, and He is generous with it.

Trust Him also with the good no one saw: the night you held your tongue, the help you gave without credit, the effort that failed. {reward}Nothing done for Him disappears; it is being grown somewhere you cannot see.{/reward} Your part is sincerity. The multiplying is His.
loving: Imagine bringing a child's drawing to someone who frames it and shows it to everyone. That is how it feels to realise Ash-Shakur values what you bring. {reward}When the One who needs nothing treasures your little, gratitude to Him becomes love, and love becomes the desire to bring more.{/reward}
now: It is payday, and after rent and bills there is barely anything left. A donation link for a well appeal comes up and five pounds feels pointless. {idea}With Ash-Shakur, five sincere pounds are a seed, not a rounding error{/idea}. Give it, forget it, and let Him grow it.
old: The good I can do is so small it hardly matters to anyone, least of all to Allah.
new: Ash-Shakur values the little I give and multiplies it beyond what I can imagine.
try: Do one small good deed today that no one will see, such as moving something harmful from a path or leaving a kind note, and tell no one.

dua.text: Ya Shakur, accept the little I bring You, and multiply it by Your generosity. Make me thankful for Your blessings and use them in what pleases You.
dua.note: Call on Him as Ash-Shakur when your efforts feel too small; the people of Paradise will praise Him by this name (35:34).

pairs.why: Ghafur Shakur: He forgives our many faults and appreciates our few good deeds, so we reach Paradise (35:34).
Shakur Halim: He multiplies the loan we give Him and is forbearing with what we fall short in (64:17).
He appreciates the outward deed and knows the intention behind it, so sincerity is what He grows (2:158).

faq.a: Ash-Shakur means the Most Appreciative. Allah does not thank out of need; He appreciates the deeds of His servants, gives worth to even the smallest of them and multiplies their reward. The root sh-k-r was used for an animal that thrived on very little fodder.

faq.q: What is the difference between Ash-Shakir and Ash-Shakur?
faq.a: Both describe Allah as appreciative. Ash-Shakir is the base form; Ash-Shakur is intensive, describing appreciation that is abundant and constant, rewarding even deeds the servant himself forgot, many times over.

faq.q: Where does Ash-Shakur appear in the Quran?
faq.a: Allah calls Himself Shakur in verses such as 35:30, 35:34 and 42:23, often paired with Ghafur, and in 64:17 paired with Halim, where charity is described as a loan to Him that He multiplies.
